description: Sync Epic documentation and Web UI copy to the self-driving lifecycle (idle/running/paused/done/closed + Start/Pause/Resume + auto-advancement). Docs/copy-only, no runtime change.

tasks.title: Rewrite docs/epics.md to the self-driving five-state lifecycle (canonical source)
tasks.description: Edit docs/epics.md in place to become the single canonical source for the self-driving Epic lifecycle. Replace the legacy active/done/closed three-state model (lifecycle section ~epics.md:141 and the field table ~epics.md:57) with the five states idle/running/paused/done/closed, each with 含义 and 进入条件; document idle as the default and done/closed as terminal. Add a Start/Pause/Resume action block covering CLI/Web UI/API with idempotency and the 'Start advances the first startable linked issue' semantics. Add an '自动推进与 running-but-idle' subsection stating auto-advancement applies only to running epics and framing running-but-idle as a situation explained by nextIssueReason (not a sixth state). Rewrite the '和 workflow 的关系' section (~epics.md:172) to replace 'Epic 只是组织工具，不参与执行' with: Epic influences advancement of linked issues, but each linked issue still runs its own workflow unchanged. Update the recommended-workflow section to match. Derive CLI examples from the real mo epic surface and HTTP examples from Api/EpicRoutes.cs.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/epics.md lifecycle section lists idle, running, paused, done, closed with meaning and entry condition for each.
docs/epics.md states a newly created Epic is idle by default and does not autonomously start until explicitly started.
docs/epics.md states done and closed are terminal states.
A scoped search of docs/epics.md finds no occurrence of `active` presented as an Epic status and the field table no longer describes status as `active / done / closed`.

docs/epics.md documents Start, Pause, Resume for CLI (mo epic start/pause/resume), Web UI (Start Epic/Pause/Resume), and HTTP API, including that Start attempts to advance the first startable linked issue, Pause is non-interrupting, Resume re-evaluates, and all three are idempotent.
docs/epics.md documents auto-advancement for running epics and explicitly states idle/paused epics do not auto-advance.
docs/epics.md describes running-but-idle as a situation explained by nextIssueReason and does NOT list it as a lifecycle state.

docs/epics.md no longer contains the phrase 'Epic 只是组织工具，不参与执行' or equivalent static-organizer framing; instead it states the Epic influences advancement of linked issues while each linked issue runs its own workflow unchanged.
CLI and HTTP examples in docs/epics.md match the real mo epic command surface and Api/EpicRoutes.cs patterns (no invented commands/endpoints).
tasks.output: docs/epics.md with rewritten lifecycle section, field table, Start/Pause/Resume block, auto-advancement/running-but-idle subsection, recommended workflow, and Epic↔workflow relationship section.
tasks.notes: This file is the canonical lifecycle source (design Decision 3); T-002..T-005 link to it, so it must land first to lock wording.

tasks.title: Update docs/concepts.md Epic framing to the self-driving planning unit
tasks.description: Update the Epic section of docs/concepts.md (~concepts.md:82, currently '一组相关 Issue 的集合') to frame the Epic as the planning + advancement unit for a product goal and its linked issues: default idle, Start begins autonomous progression. Keep it concise, link to epics.md for the full lifecycle, do not restate the state machine.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/concepts.md Epic section describes the Epic as the planning and advancement unit for a product goal (not merely a passive collection/folder).
docs/concepts.md states a new Epic is idle by default and begins autonomous progression via Start.
docs/concepts.md does not frame the Epic solely as a static collection or imply it has no role in execution.
docs/concepts.md links to epics.md for the full lifecycle rather than duplicating the state machine.
A scoped search of docs/concepts.md finds no 'active' as an Epic status and no purely-static 'collection of issues' framing as the only description.
tasks.output: docs/concepts.md Epic section rewritten with a concise self-driving framing and a link to epics.md.

tasks.title: Spot-check docs/README.md and docs/getting-started.md Epic one-liners
tasks.description: Spot-check the Epic one-liners in docs/README.md and docs/getting-started.md (currently '把零散 issue 组织成产品里程碑/路线'). Align any wording that implies the old static organizer model so it reflects Epic as the planning/advancement unit (default idle, Start to begin). Keep these as short intro pointers that link to epics.md; do not bloat them into a lifecycle description.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/README.md and docs/getting-started.md Epic one-liners do not frame the Epic purely as a static organizer/collection.
Where an Epic one-liner is updated, it is consistent with the self-driving framing in epics.md and links to epics.md for detail.
If a one-liner is already consistent or is a neutral intro pointer, it is left unchanged (no unnecessary churn).
A scoped search of docs/README.md and docs/getting-started.md finds no 'active' as an Epic status and no claim that Epic is only an organizing tool.
tasks.output: docs/README.md and docs/getting-started.md with any legacy-implying Epic one-liners aligned.
tasks.notes: Edit-on-find only; these are intro pointers so prefer a light touch.

tasks.title: Audit Web UI copy and docs for legacy-model stragglers and align
tasks.description: Run a grep-driven audit across packages/web (pages/epics, pages/epic-detail, entities/epic, features/*-epic, widgets/epic-*) and docs/ for stragglers implying the legacy model: a user-visible bare `Active` Epic status label, an ambiguous bare `Start` where the Epic lifecycle `Start Epic` is meant, or a `No linked issues` message used in a way that implies active progression. Edit-on-find only (design Decision 4): fix user-visible copy, but do NOT rename internal symbols like groupActiveEpics/ActiveEpicGroups/IssueHealth.Active (non-goal component restructuring). After any Web copy edit run npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web.
acceptanceCriteria: A grep of packages/web user-visible strings (JSX text, aria-labels, titles, toasts) finds no bare `Active` Epic status label implying the legacy active status, and no ambiguous bare `Start` where Start Epic is meant.
Any `No linked issues` (or equivalent empty-epic) copy in packages/web is consistent with the self-driving target experience and does not imply active progression.
A repo-wide grep of docs/ finds no remaining `active` as an Epic status and no remaining purely-static-organizer framing of Epic.
If any Web copy was edited, npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web both pass (the 278/279/281 tests are not broken).
If no stragglers are found, that is recorded (edit-on-find means zero edits is a valid outcome).
Internal symbol names (groupActiveEpics, ActiveEpicGroups, IssueHealth.Active, parseEpicStatus legacy mapping) are left unchanged.
tasks.output: Audit report + any user-visible copy fixes in packages/web and docs/; web typecheck and tests green if edited.
tasks.notes: Runs last so it can verify the whole docs+UI surface is mutually consistent. Primary deliverable is verification; edits only for actual stragglers.
